name: The Ritz-Carlton, Kyoto
positioning: Riverside urban hotel on the Kamogawa River in Kyoto, with a spa and Japanese-style suites
best_for: Travelers who want to walk to Gion and Teramachi

facts.text: The hotel sits on the banks of the Kamogawa River, on a site favored by Japanese nobility since the 17th century, with views of the Higashiyama Mountains.
The Gion and Teramachi districts, known for shopping and entertainment, are within walking distance of the hotel.
The hotel is a seven-level structure, two floors of which are sunken to harmonise with Kyoto's low-rise cityscape.
A waterfall flows from the upper levels of the hotel all the way down to the basement.
Some suites are Japanese-style rooms with tatami floors, futons and a deep hinoki bathtub.
Every guest room has a pruned bonsai by the window.
La Locanda serves Italian dishes made from locally sourced ingredients in a setting of wood-paneling with tatami mats.
The sushi restaurant serves Edomae-style sushi at an 11-meter-long counter decorated with Wajima lacquerware.
The hotel is home to one of the few PIERRE HERMÉ PARIS boutiques in Japan.
The wellness area has a heated indoor pool, a steam room and a dry sauna.

highlights.text: The hotel has Asia's first LA PRAIRIE SPA hotel spa.
Chef Katsuhito Inoue's chef's table is designed for an intimate group of eight guests.
Suite TSUKIMI is a penthouse retreat atop the hotel with views of the Higashiyama Mountains.
The pouch given to guests at check-in is made from old kimono textiles and reused wood from Kyoto bridge construction.

considerations.text: The hotel does not provide shuttle service.
Children under 4 years old are not allowed to use the pool.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects the luxury positioning.

sources.title: Condé Nast Traveler: The Ritz-Carlton, Kyoto
